questions.q: Why did David say the task of building the temple was great?
questions.a: The task was great, for the temple is not for people, but for Yahweh God.

questions.q: What materials did David prepare for the house of God?
questions.a: David prepared gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and valuable stones for the house of God.

questions.q: Why did David donate his personal treasure for the house of God?
questions.a: David wanted his God to have a splendid temple.

questions.q: What did David ask the people to do?
questions.a: David asked the people to contribute materials for Yahweh’s temple.

questions.q: What gifts were offered by the leaders of the ancestors’ families?
questions.a: They made freewill offerings.

questions.q: What did the leaders give for the service of the house of God?
questions.a: They gave gold, silver, bronze, and iron.

questions.q: Who guarded the stones given for the house of Yahweh?
questions.a: Jehiel the Gershonite guarded the storeroom for these stones.

questions.q: Why did the people rejoice for the freewill offerings?
questions.a: They rejoiced because they had contributed wholeheartedly to Yahweh.

questions.q: What did David do in front of all the assembly?
questions.a: David blessed and praised Yahweh in front of all the assembly.

questions.q: What does David say belongs to Yahweh?
questions.a: All of creation is Yahweh’s, as well as the majesty, the glory, and the might.

questions.q: How is Yahweh able to make people great and give them strength?
questions.a: He possesses strength and might and is able to give strength to anyone.

questions.q: What did David say the people were doing for God?
questions.a: David said they were thanking and praising God.

questions.q: What did David say about the things the people gave to Yahweh?
questions.a: David said that all things come from Yahweh, and they had simply given back to him what was his.

questions.q: What did David say their days on earth were like?
questions.a: David said their days on earth were like a shadow, passing quickly.

questions.q: According to David, where did all the materials for the temple come from?
questions.a: All the materials for the temple came from Yahweh’s hand.

questions.q: In what does God have pleasure when he examines the heart?
questions.a: Yahweh examines the heart and has pleasure in uprightness.

questions.q: What made David look with joy on God’s people who were present?
questions.a: He looked with joy as they willingly offered gifts to Yahweh.

questions.q: Whose God did David say Yahweh was?
questions.a: David said Yahweh was the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel (Jacob), their ancestors.

questions.q: What did David ask Yahweh to give Solomon?
questions.a: David asked Yahweh to give Solomon a wholehearted desire to obey his commands and to build the temple.

questions.q: How did all the assembly bless and worship Yahweh?
questions.a: All the assembly praised Yahweh and bowed down and worshiped him.

questions.q: How many bulls, rams, and lambs did the people offer to Yahweh?
questions.a: They offered 1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams, and 1,000 lambs.

questions.q: With whose authority did they anoint Solomon to be ruler?
questions.a: They anointed him with olive oil to show that Yahweh had chosen him to be king.

questions.q: Who did Solomon succeed as king?
questions.a: Solomon succeeded his father, David as king.

questions.q: Who supported Solomon as king?
questions.a: All the leaders, the warriors, and David’s other sons supported Solomon as king.

questions.q: How did Yahweh greatly honor Solomon before all Israel?
questions.a: He bestowed on him greater power than he had ever given to any king before him in Israel.

questions.q: Whose son was David?
questions.a: David was the son of Jesse.

questions.q: How many years did David reign over Israel?
questions.a: David reigned over Israel for 40 years.

questions.q: What two things had David enjoyed during his long life?
questions.a: He enjoyed wealth and honor.

questions.q: Who wrote the records about the events of King David’s reign?
questions.a: Samuel, Nathan, and Gad wrote the records about King David’s reign.

commentary.text: David induces the princes and people to offer willingly.

Verses 1–9 What is done in works of piety and charity, should be done willingly, not by constraint; for God loves a cheerful giver. David set a good example. This David offered, not from constraint, or for show; but because he had set his affection to the house of God, and thought he could never do enough towards promoting that good work. Those who would draw others to good, must lead the way themselves.

We cannot form a right idea of the magnificence of the temple, and the buildings around it, about which such quantities of gold and silver were employed. But the unsearchable riches of Christ exceed the splendour of the temple, infinitely more than that surpassed the meanest cottage on earth. Instead of boasting of these large oblations, David gave solemn thanks to the Lord. All they gave for the Lord's temple was his own; if they attempted to keep it, death would soon have removed them from it. The only use they could make of it to their real advantage, was, to consecrate it to the service of Him who gave it.

This great assembly joined with David in adoring God. Whoever is the mouth of the congregation, those only have the benefit who join him, not by bowing down the head, so much as by lifting up the soul. Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord. Solomon's kingdom typified the kingdom of the Messiah, whose throne is the throne of the Lord.

When we read the second book of Samuel, we could scarcely have expected to behold David appear so illustrious in his closing scene. But his repentance had been as remarkable as his sin; and his conduct during his afflictions, and towards the end of his life, appears to have had a good effect on his subjects. Blessed be God, even the chief of sinners may hope for a glorious departure, when brought to repent and flee for refuge to the Saviour's atoning blood. Let us mark the difference between the spirit and character of the man after God's own heart, living and dying, and those of worthless professors, who resemble him in nothing but their sins, and who wickedly try to excuse their crimes by his sins. Let us watch and pray, lest we be overcome by temptation, and overtaken by sin, to the dishonour of God, and the wounding of our own consciences. When we feel that we have offended, let us follow David's example of repentance and patience, looking for a glorious resurrection, through our Lord Jesus Christ.
